is a preliminary cost estimation report prepared before vessel arrival or before the port agency job is executed. This report provides an estimated breakdown of port charges, agency fees, service costs, and other operational expenses required for the vessel call. EPDA is used as the basis for customer approval and advance payment request.

The Final Disbursement Account (FDA) is a final cost statement generated after the port agency job has been completed. The report summarizes all actual charges incurred during the vessel call, including port charges, agency fees, vendor costs, authority charges, taxes, and other operational expenses. FDA also records any prefunding or advance payment received from the customer/principal and calculates the final outstanding amount or settlement balance. This report is used as the basis for final billing, settlement confirmation, and job closing.

The Payment Request & Authorisation Form is an internal finance document used to request, approve, and process payments related to port agency operational activities. The form contains payment request details such as payee, request date, due date, payment purpose, requesting department, payment method, recipient bank information, itemized payment details, job reference, and total amount. It also includes approval, payment processing, and ledger posting sections to support finance verification, payment authorization, payment execution, and accounting allocation to the related job or principal.

The Credit Facility Prefunding Vendor Form is an internal finance document used to request, approve, and process prefunding payments to vendors or related parties for port agency operational costs. The form contains payment request details such as payee, request date, due date, payment purpose, department, payment method, bank account information, itemized cost details, job reference, and total amount. It also includes approval, payment processing, and ledger posting sections to support finance validation, payment execution, accounting entry, and cost allocation to the related job or principal.

The Cargo Manifest is a report containing detailed information of cargo carried by the vessel, including cargo description, quantity, shipper, consignee, loading port, discharge port, and other relevant cargo details. This document is commonly used for customs, port authority, and operational reference during cargo handling activities.

The Statement of Fact (SOF) is an operational report that records the chronological sequence of vessel activities during the port call. It includes key timestamps such as vessel arrival, berthing, commencement and completion of cargo operations, shifting, unberthing, and departure. SOF is used as an official operational reference for performance review, dispute handling, and billing support.

The Shipping Order is a document issued to confirm cargo shipment instructions and authorize the arrangement of cargo movement or loading activities. This report typically contains shipper information, consignee, vessel details, cargo details, destination, and shipping instruction. It is used as an operational reference for shipment execution and coordination with related parties.
Gross Weight / Quantity of the cargo

The Stowage Plan is a report that shows the planned arrangement and placement of cargo on board the vessel. It provides information on cargo location, quantity, weight distribution, and loading sequence. This document is used to support safe cargo handling, vessel stability, and efficient loading or discharging operations.

Principal sends payment confirmation and transfer receipt to Operations after completing the payment.
Confirmation may be sent by email or other agreed communication channel.
Operations receives the transfer receipt or payment confirmation from the Principal and verifies the information against the related prefund invoice.
Operations should ensure the payment proof matches the invoice number, amount, and customer.
Attach Transfer Receipt and Confirm to Finance
Operations attaches the transfer receipt to the related prefund request or jobsheet, then informs Finance to proceed with payment registration.
System should allow attachment of transfer receipt and notification to Finance.
Finance Officer registers the customer payment in the system based on the confirmed transfer receipt. The payment settles the outstanding prefund invoice.
Journal impact: Dr Bank, Cr Account Receivable.

This scenario occurs when a port agency job has already been initiated or is currently in progress, but the customer unexpectedly cancels the service before any prefund, advance payment, or down payment has been received.
Principal sends a confirmation or formal request to cancel the port agency job that has already been initiated or planned.
Confirmation may be sent via email or other agreed communication channel.
team receives and reviews the cancellation confirmation from the Principal, then identifies that the job is cancelled without any prefund or advance payment received.
Ops must verify the related job reference before proceeding with cancellation.

team cancels the related jobsheet in the system and records the cancellation reason. Since no prefund has been received, the cancellation will proceed by generating a cancellation fee charge to the customer.
System should allow cancellation status and cancellation reason to be recorded in the jobsheet.

Finance creates a customer invoice for the applicable cancellation fee based on the cancelled jobsheet. The invoice will recognize the cancellation fee as revenue and create an account receivable from the customer.
Journal impact: Dr Account Receivable, Cr Revenue, and recognition of accrued expense if applicable.
Finance records the customer payment once the cancellation fee has been received. The payment will settle the outstanding invoice and update the receivable balance.
Journal impact: Dr Bank, Cr Account Receivable.
